text:
Priya: FYI escalation from ACME (on-prem/private). Their agent reports intermittent failures when calling our private control plane. Errors: "TLS handshake failure", "certificate verify failed", and sometimes "407 Proxy Authentication Required". Can SRE take a look?

SupportBot: Automated alert attached: agent-id=acme-edge-12, last_success=2026-03-12T08:13:21Z, error_sample="ssl: certificate signed by unknown authority"

Mike: Thanks — can you paste the minimal repro from their edge host? Also confirm if they're behind an explicit HTTP proxy or a transparent proxy/firewall.

Priya: Customer provided a short repro. Running from their edge node: 

```
$ curl -v https://control-plane.redwood.internal/health
* Connected to proxy.company.local (10.10.1.5) port 8080 (#0)
* Proxy replied: 407 Proxy Authentication Required
* Closing connection 0
curl: (56) Received HTTP code 407 from proxy after CONNECT
```

Then they tried with proxy auth (they have a token) and got TLS verify errors:

```
$ curl -v -x http://user:token@proxy.company.local:8080 https://control-plane.redwood.internal/health
* Connected to proxy.company.local (10.10.1.5) port 8080 (#0)
* Establish HTTP proxy tunnel to control-plane.redwood.internal:443
* TLS handshake failed
* SSL certificate problem: certificate is not trusted
```

And an openssl check returned the proxy's cert chain (subject CN=Corporate Proxy Root) instead of the real control plane cert.

Mike: Sounds like an SSL-terminating proxy (MITM) that replaces certs. Two quick angles: 1) proxy requires auth/NTLM and may not allow CONNECT passthrough, 2) proxy is doing TLS interception with an org CA not trusted by the agent runtime.

Alice: Checklist I usually ask for:
- Can the proxy do HTTP CONNECT to arbitrary host:443? (some proxies only allow CONNECT to a short allowlist)
- Is the agent using system truststore or a bundled jre cacerts? We need the proxy CA installed there.
- Does the proxy rewrite SNI or terminate TLS (we saw cert CN mismatch, so looks like termination).
- DNS resolution: are they resolving control-plane.redwood.internal to an internal IP that then goes through proxy?

Mike: Repro commands to ask the customer to paste back (run from the same host as the failing agent):

```
# check raw TCP connectivity
$ nc -vz control-plane.redwood.internal 443

# check traceroute
$ traceroute -n control-plane.redwood.internal

# inspect TLS chain presented by endpoint
$ openssl s_client -connect control-plane.redwood.internal:443 -servername control-plane.redwood.internal -showcerts

# curl via proxy (verbose)
$ curl -v -x http://proxy.company.local:8080 https://control-plane.redwood.internal/health
```

Priya: They sent back the openssl output — it shows the proxy CA in the chain and the cert subject is proxy.company.local, not our CN. They also included their proxy vendor: Squid with NTLM helper.

Mike: That explains it. Two paths: 1) get their proxy to allow CONNECT passthrough for control-plane.redwood.internal (recommended), or 2) add the proxy CA to the agent runtime truststore so the agent accepts the intercepted cert. The tradeoffs: (1) preserves end-to-end TLS and SNI so we can verify identity; (2) requires them to trust the proxy CA across workloads (security implications).

Alice: Also verify no_proxy/NO_PROXY is set for the control-plane host in the agent environment if they have a route that bypasses proxy. If they can route directly from the subnet to our control-plane IPs, that's easiest (firewall permitting outbound 443 to our FQDN/IPs).

Priya: I pushed the commands above. Customer tried option (2) first: added proxy CA to system store and restarted the agent. Still failing intermittently. Their logs show occasional SNI rewrite upstream which breaks virtual host routing on our side.

Mike: If the proxy rewrites SNI or terminates and then initiates a new TLS session with a different SNI, we can't rely on hostname verification even with CA trusted. So option (1) is preferred: ask the proxy team to create an allowlist entry that forwards CONNECT to control-plane.redwood.internal without terminating TLS.

Priya: Customer's proxy team changed the Squid rules to allow CONNECT passthrough for control-plane.redwood.internal and removed header rewrites for that host. They also added the control-plane FQDN to the proxy's allowlist. After that the agent reports healthy.

EngOncall: Adding for runbook updates: we should add a short checklist to support docs for private/on-prem customers: 1) Ensure outbound 443 to control-plane FQDN/IPs is allowed, 2) If using an HTTP proxy, confirm it supports CONNECT passthrough to target host:443, 3) If proxy intercepts TLS, customer must either install proxy CA in agent truststore OR (preferred) configure passthrough for our FQDN, 4) Ensure DNS resolves to the expected internal/external IPs and that SNI is preserved.

Mike: I'll create a small KB with the exact curl/openssl/nc commands and suggested firewall/proxy rules. Priya — can you paste the customer's final confirmation so I can link it in the KB?

Priya: Customer confirmed resolution at 2026-03-12T09:25Z: "Squid proxy updated to allow CONNECT for control-plane.redwood.internal, TLS passthrough enabled, agent now able to reach control plane. No code changes required." :white_check_mark: 

Priya: Closing the escalation. Follow-up: we should add a troubleshooting snippet in the private deployment quickstart about proxy CA vs passthrough and include sample openssl/curl outputs to help customers identify MITM issues quickly.
